draft.title: Gender roles and identity
card: A gender role is a set of expectations about how people of a gender should behave, dress or work. A society teaches these expectations to its members.
People learn gender roles from family, peers, schools and the media. Praise, teasing and example all shape what a person thinks is expected of them.
Gender roles are not fixed. They change over time within a society, and they differ between cultures.
Gender identity is a person's own sense of their gender. It can match the expectations placed on them or differ from them, and it is part of how they see themselves.
draft.remember: Gender roles are learned expectations that vary across time and cultures. Gender identity is a person's own sense of their gender.

a.q: Which example best shows that gender roles change over time?
opts: Women in Australia now work in many jobs once held by men
A boy in Perth plays the same sport as his father
Two cousins in different countries wear different clothes
A girl in Cairns says she feels confident about who she is
a.why: The same society expects something different now than it did in the past, so the role has changed over time. Clothing in different countries shows a difference between cultures, not a change over time.
a.clue: Look for the same society at two different times.

b.q: Sam grows up in a town where boys are expected to hide their feelings. Sam moves to a country where boys are encouraged to talk about them. What does this best show?
opts: Gender identity is decided by the family
Gender roles are the same in every society
Gender roles are not learned by young people
b.why: Two societies teach different expectations for boys, so gender roles differ between cultures. It does not show that the family decides gender identity, because identity is a person's own sense of their gender and the case does not describe it.
b.clue: Compare what the two places expect of boys.

a.best: Women in Australia now work in many jobs once held by men
